## What this case checks

Provide a canonical multipolygon encoded as WKB so format-specific loader behavior can be compared directly against the GeoJSON baseline.

## Risk types covered

- [`format_comparison`](../risk/format-comparison.md)

| `required_drivers` | none &mdash; no OGR driver opens this format (use shapely) |

## Notes

### Purpose
Tests MultiPolygon geometry loading from binary WKB file.

### Data
- Geometry: `MULTIPOLYGON (((10 50, 10.5 50, 10.5 50.5, 10 50.5, 10 50)), ((11 50, 11.5 50, 11.5 50.5, 11 50.5, 11 50)))`
- Attributes: none. The format has no attribute slot;
  `VectorCase.load()` synthesizes a single `name` = `multipolygon_wkb_baseline` row.
- Feature count: 1

### Validation
- Geometry type: `MultiPolygon`
- CRS: `EPSG:4326`, supplied by `case.yaml` — the format stores none
- Geometry equals `simple_valid_multipolygon` under `shapely.normalize`, which is how
  `tests/unit/test_cross_format_canonical.py` compares them. The comparison is
  winding-insensitive by necessity: the Shapefile specification mandates the
  opposite ring orientation from RFC 7946, and OGR rewrites winding on write.
  Orientation itself is asserted by `shapefile_ring_orientation`.

### Generation
Generated by `scripts/generate_vector_fixtures.py` — do not hand-edit. The
geometry is derived from `params.canonical_source_case_id`
(`simple_valid_multipolygon`), and `generate_vector_fixtures.py --check` fails on any drift.
